name: Question 2
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-1\,,\,{t}^{3}+1⟩,t\in (-\infty ,0)$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨2\,,\,1⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1)\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t\,,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $⟨2\,,\,1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨2\,,\,1⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨2\,,\,1⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨2\,,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨2t\,,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ & =0 \\ 2\cdot 2t+1\cdot 3{t}^{2} & =0 \\ 4t+3{t}^{2} & =0 \\ t(4+3t) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (-\infty ,0)$, the only solution is $t=-\frac{4}{3}$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-\frac{4}{3}) & =⟨{(-\frac{4}{3})}^{2}-1\,,\,{(-\frac{4}{3})}^{3}+1⟩=⟨\frac{7}{9}\,,\,-\frac{37}{27}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $⟨2\,,\,-1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(\frac{7}{9}\,,\,-\frac{37}{27}).$

Question 2
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨t2−1,t3+1⟩,t∈(−∞,0) find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector ⟨2,1⟩.

a
 (0,0)
b
 (3,−7) and (79,−3727)
c
 (79,−3727)
d
 (0,0) and (43,169)
e
 (43,169)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(t2−1),ddt(t3+1)⟩=⟨2t,3t2⟩

The vectors ⟨2,1⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular for some value of the parameter t if and only if ⟨2,1⟩⋅r′(t)=0. So, we have

⟨2,1⟩⋅r′(t)=0⟨2,1⟩⋅⟨2t,3t2⟩=02⋅2t+1⋅3t2=04t+3t2=0t(4+3t)=0.

Since t∈(−∞,0), the only solution is t=−43

Finally, since

r(−43)=⟨(−43)2−1,(−43)3+1⟩=⟨79,−3727⟩,

we conclude that ⟨2,−1⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular at the point (79,−3727).
